Plain Text Files
Part 1: Manipulating
Strings
Plain Text Files are made up entirely of
strings. To use them effectively, you
need to know how to manipulate strings
effectively.

Plain Text Files Use String Values
Plain text files store information as text, so Python
reads their contents as strings.
Even if a file contains numbers, those values initially
behave like text until they are converted to another
data type.
Understanding common string methods makes it
easier to clean, separate, modify, and convert data
read from files.

lower() upper() capitalize() title()
/ / /

text.

lowercase, while upper()

capitalize() capitalizes the
first character, and title() print(text.title())

each word.
